item.research_question: How can multimetal high entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles be synthesized and decorated onto few-layer graphene, and does this composite exhibit superior corrosion resistance compared to graphene-only or bare substrates?
item.material_system: NiFeCrCoCu high entropy alloy nanoparticles decorated on few-layer graphene (HEA-Gr)
item.processing_route: Two-step method: (1) Mechanical milling of 4 g graphite powder with elemental blend (0.193 g Fe, 0.180 g Cr, 0.204 g Co, 0.220 g Cu, 0.203 g Ni) in toluene for 80 hours with a 20:1 ball-to-powder weight ratio; (2) Sonication of the milled composite in 10 ml ethanol with 20 mg sodium lauryl sulphate (SLS) for 2 hours, followed by centrifugation at 8000 rpm to remove SLS.
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl solution at room temperature using a three-electrode cell (working electrode: HEA-Gr/epoxy coated mild steel, counter: platinum foil, reference: Ag/AgCl); potentiodynamic polarization from ±200 mV vs OCP at 1 mVs⁻¹; EIS from 100 kHz to 0.01 Hz with 5 mV amplitude.
key_findings: Average nanoparticle size was 8 ± 2 nm with an average graphene thickness of 3.3 ± 0.9 nm.
The nanoparticles exhibited a face centred cubic (fcc) structure with a lattice parameter of 3.394 Å.
Total polarization resistance (Rp) for the HEA-Gr composite-epoxy coating was 19650 Ω, significantly higher than bare MS (903.9 Ω) and graphene-epoxy coated MS (5843 Ω).
The HEA-Gr composite showed a positive shift in corrosion potential (Ecorr) and decreased corrosion current density (Icorr) compared to all control samples.
STEM-EDS analysis confirmed all five component metal atoms (Fe, Cr, Co, Cu, Ni) were uniformly distributed within individual nanoparticles.
A large distribution in composition between individual nanoparticles was observed, with Ni present in the lowest amount in a large fraction of particles.
item.mechanism: Strain caused by the presence of nanoparticles within the inter-layer spacing of graphite facilitated the exfoliation process during sonication. The resulting HEA nanoparticles form a protective layer that significantly reduces surface activity towards the corrosion environment, enhancing the barrier properties beyond what graphene alone provides.
item.limitations: The text notes a large distribution in the composition between the nanoparticles, with Cr showing a relatively wider distribution and Ni often present in the lowest amounts, suggesting compositional heterogeneity at the single-particle level.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the as-synthesised HEA nanoparticle-graphene composite can be spray painted over surfaces to provide enhanced corrosion protection.
quotes: Strain caused due to the presence of nanoparticles within the inter-layer spacing facilitated the exfoliation process during the subsequent sonication of the multimetal-graphite powder resulting in the formation of HEA nanoparticle decorated graphene.

Total Rp i.e. Rp = Rcoat + Rct was found to be 903.9 Ω, 1339 Ω, 5843 Ω and 19650 Ω for bare MS, epoxy coated MS, graphene-epoxy coated MS and HEA-Gr composite-epoxy coated MS substrate samples respectively.
The as-synthesised HEA nanoparticle-graphene composite exhibited high corrosion resistance performance making then a suitable materials for corrosion protection application.
